sentences.text: Revenue, net interest income plus noninterest income, rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, a 7.3% CAGR [D5][D206].
The path was a step change rather than steady compounding: revenue grew 22.9% in FY2023 and 12.3% in FY2024, against 1.4% in FY2021 [D179][D202][D129].
The FY2023 step came from net interest income, up 33.8% to $89.3 billion, as higher rates expanded deposit margins [D174][F8][P37].
Net income compounded at 9.7% over the window, faster than revenue, and EPS diluted at 13.9% as the share count fell [F113][F115].
North America supplied 76.6% of FY2025 revenue but only +0.2pp of its growth, while Asia-Pacific contributed +1.2pp on 17.3% growth [D249][D251][D300][D301].
FY2025 net interest income rose 3.1% to $95.4 billion on higher Markets net interest income and higher Card Services revolving balances, largely offset by deposit margin compression [D221][F10][P28].
Noninterest income grew only 2.4% to $87.0 billion, held back by the absence of the $7.9 billion Visa share gain recorded in FY2024 [D222][F20][P27].
Operating costs grew 1.4pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 4.2%, so the incremental margin stayed positive [D225][D226].
Net income fell 2.6% while diluted EPS rose 1.4%, the gap set by a 3.4% reduction in diluted shares [D214][D216][D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, below the 57.2% window median and above the 51.7% window low of FY2024 [D207][D333][D331].
Against seven bank peers the efficiency ratio sat at the 0th percentile versus a 61.7% peer median [D336][D337].
Noninterest expense rose 4.2% to $95.6 billion on higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, and technology and marketing investment [D225][X137][P26].
The credit-loss provision reached 7.8% of revenue in FY2025, above the 6.0% peer median, as the provision rose to $14.2 billion [D208][D341][X147].
Net margin of 31.2% sat 21.1pp below the 52.3% net interest income share of revenue, with the provision and expense the main claims on it [D210][D209].
Operating cash flow was an outflow of $147.8 billion in FY2025, or -2.59x net income, against an inflow of $78.1 billion in FY2021 [F60][D204][F56].
The FY2025 outflow came from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, and net loan originations held for sale [P21].
For a bank, operating cash flow mostly reflects balance-sheet movement rather than earnings quality, so the negative conversion is not a signal about profitability.
Stock-based compensation of $3.6 billion was small against the $95.6 billion expense base, so it does not distort the cash picture [X50][X137].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, at the 100th percentile of seven bank peers against an 11.8% peer median [D213][D338][D339].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits, up from 43.1% in FY2021 as balance-sheet capacity was put to work [D211][D115].
Loans rose $121.1 billion, driven by CIB Markets and AWM securities-based lending on higher client demand [P4].
Buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion in FY2025 exceeded the $31.6 billion of repurchases alone, and the diluted share count fell 3.4% [D205][X102][D224].
FY2021 to FY2025 net income in the table comes from the proxy pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, and differs by up to 0.10% [R1][F26][X16][F30][X20].
The gap is immaterial to any trend here, but the 10-K figures should be used where precision matters [R1].
FY2020 pretax income and tax were later restated to $35.8 billion and $6.7 billion from $35.4 billion and $6.3 billion first reported [R2][R3][X63][X73].
The restatement shifts FY2020 net income slightly but does not change the shape of the FY2020 trough [R2][R3].
Whether the efficiency ratio holds below the 57.2% window median in the FY2026 10-K will show if the cost discipline of FY2024 and FY2025 persists [D333][D207].
Whether the credit-loss provision stays above the 6.0% peer median, from 7.8% of revenue in FY2025, will test the credit cycle [D208][D341].
Whether net interest income growth recovers from 3.1% in FY2025, with deposit margin compression cited, will show if the rate-driven step is fading [D221][P28].
